sections.label: Changi Airport passenger traffic recovery
sections.summary: Changi Airport passenger traffic has recovered to about 80% of pre-COVID levels and is expected to recover fully by 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Changi Airport’s passenger traffic has recovered to about 80% of pre-COVID levels; passenger traffic is expected to recover fully by 2024.

sections.label: Aviation and maritime infrastructure expansion
sections.summary: The Government has planned major aviation and maritime infrastructure expansions over the next two decades and restarted the Changi Airport Terminal 5 project, targeted to be operational in the mid-2030s.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The Government has planned major expansions in our aviation and maritime infrastructure over the next two decades.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: We have restarted the Changi Airport Terminal 5 (T5) project, which is targeted to be operational in the mid-2030s.

sections.label: Tuas Port opening and completion
sections.summary: Tuas Port opened as planned despite the pandemic and is on track to be completed by the 2040s, with an annual handling capacity of 65 million twenty-foot equivalent units.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Tuas Port opened as planned despite the pandemic and is on track to be completed by the 2040s, with an annual handling capacity of 65 million twenty-foot equivalent units.

sections.label: Cleaner energy airside vehicles
sections.summary: MOT will aim for all airside vehicles at Changi Airport to run on cleaner energy by 2040 and will require all new airside light vehicles, forklifts, and tractors to be electric from 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: MOT will aim for all airside vehicles at Changi Airport to run on cleaner energy by 2040, and will require all new airside light vehicles, forklifts, and tractors to be electric from 2025 as part of the transition.

sections.label: EV chargers and pedestrian-friendly streets
sections.summary: EV charger deployment has been brought forward, with one in three public housing carparks to have charging points by end of this year and full coverage by 2025, while pedestrian-friendly initiatives will expand and Friendly Streets will be piloted in five neighbourhoods.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: We have brought forward the island-wide deployment of Electric Vehicle (EV) chargers, and one in three public housing carparks will have EV charging points by the end of this year, with full coverage by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: We remain on track to deploy 60,000 charging points by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: To make our streets more conducive for pedestrians, we will expand pedestrian-friendly initiatives, such as retrofitting lifts at pedestrian overhead bridges, providing covered linkways, and traffic-calming schemes such as Silver Zones and School Zones.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: We will work with local stakeholders to pilot Friendly Streets in five neighbourhoods, in areas near key amenities with high pedestrian flow.

sections.label: Cycling path network expansion
sections.summary: Friendly Streets will complement the expansion of the cycling path network to about 1,300 kilometres by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Friendly Streets will complement the expansion of our network of cycling paths to about 1,300 kilometres by 2030.
